body:
Credit @sublatesublate-design for the report and the log. I read the whole antigravity request path at upstream/main (1e1068c86) against your log. The short version: every shape in your log maps to the upstream (or your machine's network path) going quiet, and the two bounds you hit are deliberate ones — magpie's own time in the observed request was 20 ms of a 135 s turn. I found no defect on magpie's side to fix; below is the mechanism, what each log line was, and the one policy question this leaves open for the maintainer.

## What magpie does on this path today

The streaming turn to `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` goes out on the gateway's shared vendor transport (`internal/gateway/upstream_transport.go`):

- The vendor gets **10 minutes** to send response headers (`upstreamHeaderWait`), deliberately generous: a reply that arrives in one burst at the end of a long generation runs past 10 minutes (that bound was last revisited in 13f658a37, youyo.p).
- A silent HTTP/2 connection is **pinged after 20 s and dropped if the ping is unanswered for 10 s** (`netproxy.HTTP2Health`, #2843). A live vendor answers pings whatever its streams are doing, so a long wait for a first byte is never cut by it.
- While a try holds with nothing heard, the agent is kept alive with SSE comments from 3 s in, at most one every 5 s (`holdWriter.keepAlive`), for up to 5 minutes of total silence (`keepaliveLongest`); past that the stream is left "for a timeout to end".
- After the upstream's 200, if the stream then says nothing, magpie keeps the client alive for up to **30 minutes** (`keepThroughSilence`, `translatedQuietLongest`), and for Anthropic clients sends a ping event once a minute (`pingEvery`) — Claude Code's 300 s stream watchdog resets on pings.
- A reply that says nothing is a failure, asked again in place up to `streamRetries` (2) before it surfaces as `502 ... an empty reply (the model answered nothing; try again)` (#667). A stream that dies mid-reply is said so in the client's own protocol (`cutMidReply`), again after bounded in-place retries.
- A kept-alive connection dropped before the request was sent is replayed at once on a new one (#2136); a new connection closed unsent is retried, then failed with an error that says to check the proxy/VPN. The per-provider RPM limiter waits only for a minute-window slot before sending — an in-flight stuck request never holds later requests.
- Your Questions asked for separate timings — magpie already records them per try, and your report quotes them: `Wait` is the vendor's own time from request written to its first byte, `Head` the connection's share, TTFT the time to first content (nettrace, surfaced as `ttft_ms` in usage/route events and `magpie.ttft_ms` in OTel).

The request itself is shaped as the Antigravity client's: `project`, `userAgent: "antigravity"`, `requestType: "agent"`, a per-request `requestId`, a per-conversation `sessionId`, and `User-Agent: antigravity/hub/<latest>` (`codeAssistEnvelope`, `googleApp.userAgent`). Nothing in it plausibly queues differently from `agy`'s.

## What each line in your log was

- **200, TTFT 134 s** — the connection was fine (connect/send 1 s, magpie internal 20 ms); Google held the request 134 s before its first content. Entirely upstream.
- **499 after ~4m59.9–5m0.1 (four of them)** — your agent hung up, not magpie (magpie records 499 when the client disconnects; its own bound was still 10 minutes away). The timing matches a ~300 s client stream watchdog. During the pre-first-byte wait magpie can keep the stream alive only with comments: Anthropic ping events before `message_start` are forbidden — the SDKs fail with "Unexpected event order, got ping before message_start" (`anthropicEncoder.keepalive`) — and comments do not reset that watchdog. So an agent with a 300 s event-based watchdog cuts a queued turn at ~5 m regardless of what magpie sends.
- **502 "an empty reply" after 1m58.7s** — the upstream answered with a reply that said nothing; magpie had already asked again in place before surfacing the 502 with the try-again text (#667).
- **502 "unexpected EOF" after 4m22–4m54** — the connection died mid-wait or mid-reply after minutes of upstream silence; magpie surfaced it as a retryable error in the client's protocol.
- **TLS handshake timeouts on the model list** — those requests share the same proxy decision and transport family (`netproxy`), so they point at your machine's path to googleapis being degraded that day, independently of the streaming call.

## Hypotheses vs evidence

| Hypothesis | Evidence for | Evidence against | Prediction if true |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H1: Antigravity upstream queueing for gemini-3.8-flash (reasoning high) | 200 with TTFT 134 s while magpie spent 20 ms; empty replies and late EOFs repeating over 7 h; the h2 ping would have dropped a dead connection at ≤30 s, yet these requests ran 2–5 m — a live connection whose backend was silent | none found statically | A retry on a fresh connection in the same minute stalls too; `agy` at peak would occasionally stall the same way |
| H2: your proxy/VPN path degraded | model-list TLS handshake timeouts share the same proxy path; "unexpected EOF" after minutes of silence is the shape #2136 and the unsent-retry work were built for | not verifiable statically | Stalls correlate with the proxy; running the provider with proxy "direct" (or another proxy) changes the pattern |
| H3: magpie stalls (no timeout, buffering, head-of-line) | — | internal time 20 ms; the 10-min header bound exists; the RPM limiter never queues behind an in-flight request; keepalives go out from 3 s | Refuted |
| H4: stale reused h2 connection (#2843 family) | family history | ping health (landed 2026-10-19) drops a silent connection at ≤30 s; observed waits ran minutes and ended 200 | Refuted for this report |
| H5: magpie cancelled the 499s | — | 499 is the client's disconnect; magpie's own bound was 10 m | Refuted — the agent's own ~300 s watchdog did it |

H1 and H2 are not exclusive; both say the wait is outside magpie.

## For the maintainer

Same machinery serves Gemini/Vertex (`emptyFails` covers CodeAssist and Gemini alike; one shared vendor transport), so this is not antigravity-specific.

- **Option A — no change.** The bounds are deliberate and recent (10-min header wait; 30-min post-200 silence; ping health #2843; replay #2136). This report's data shows magpie doing what it was built to do; the 2–5 minute stalls end at the agent's own watchdog or a retryable 502.
- **Option B — a shorter TTFT bound for CodeAssist.** Cut a header-less try at, say, 3–5 minutes and ask once more on a fresh connection or the next account, so the agent gets the retry before its own watchdog fires. The cost is real: Google may still be queueing the first try, so the retry can bill the turn twice, and legitimate slow prefills get cut. A policy call, and it moves Gemini/Vertex with it.

## Not verified

No Windows/antigravity environment here — everything above is a code read plus your log. Unknown: whether `agy` went through the same proxy, account and minutes; your proxy setup at all; and whether the 134 s wait was Google queueing or your path stalling — the timings magpie already records (Wait vs Head vs TTFT per try) separate those, as does a try with the provider's proxy set to "direct".

AI use: comment written with GLM-5.3-Flash (ZCode) from a code-level read of the repo at 1e1068c86; no requests were sent to the upstream.
